claim: Qwen2.5-VL aims to read visual information at useful resolution without paying full global-attention cost in every vision layer. It also gives video positions a clock, rather than treating the third frame at every sampling rate as the same moment.

claim:
- **Windowed vision preserves resolution.** Most ViT layers attend locally; periodic full-attention layers exchange information across the image.
- **Video positions follow elapsed time.** Dynamic FPS training is paired with absolute-time temporal MRoPE positions.
- **Outputs become structured evidence.** Training covers document HTML, tables, chart data, grounded coordinates and action formats, rather than only fluent captions.

claim: [Figure 1](#figure-1) is best read from pixels upward. The processor resizes while retaining aspect ratio within pixel bounds and makes spatial dimensions compatible with patching and merging. A 3D convolution embeds 2×14×14 tubes. Still images are handled with repeated frames for the temporal patching interface. The ViT performs local/global visual computation; four neighboring spatial features are concatenated and projected to language width. They replace the corresponding image/video placeholder positions in the language embeddings.

claim: The inspected get_rope_index path converts seconds-per-grid to the integer dtype of its arange tensor before multiplying. A duration below one second can therefore truncate to zero in that version. At the common 2 FPS setting, a two-frame tube lasts one second and avoids that particular case; at 4 FPS it lasts half a second. This is a code-inspection finding, not an executed regression test. The report's intended variable-FPS method and a version-specific runtime path must not be conflated.

claim: Dynamic resolution means token cost changes with the input. The inspected processor defaults range from 3,136 to 12,845,056 pixels, corresponding to roughly four to 16,384 merged spatial tokens per image before markers, because each token represents 28×28 pixels. Actual resizing and rounding determine the final count. Multiple large images compete with text, video and output for the same decoder context.
